Reform UK MP says policies left a ‘deep scar’ on communities

These are from my colleague Peter Walker, who was at the Tory event where James Cleverly was named as the party’s candidate for London mayor.

Peter posted this before the result was announced.

Khan (who may or may not stand a 4th time) has thus far faced a dilettante who decided to campaign on a racist platform (Zack Goldsmith) and two oddballs in Shaun Bailey and then Susan Hall. Not even he can be lucky yet again

Interesting that [the Conservatives] did not say how many votes were cast, just the percentage - which perhaps indicates it was not a huge number

Cleverly’s speech is mainly an attack on Labour and Khan, which is likely to be a theme for his campaign: “Burnham can’t stand London and Khan stand up to Burnham.” Also a pitch about building houses and cutting crime, and boosting transport.

Cleverly says he would “end Khan’s war on motorists”, which is a sign he might lean into the anti-cycling and walking rhetoric which the London Tories have a habit of espousing. Expect talk about LTNs and 20mph zones.

In the media Q&A Cleverly is pinned down on whether he backs the Tory party line on wanting to leave the ECHR and opposes net zero. He confirms he does (as he has to). Such things will be ready ammunition for Labour.

Cleverly says of Andy Burnham, “His residual behaviour is to be anti-London”. This will very much be a theme of his campaign, it seems. Not sure how resonant a “poor London!” message will be even in London

People are leaving London, or not choosing to come here in the first place, businesses, job creators, families leaving London, and by the time of the election in 2028, Khan will have been mayor for 12 years, and those two things are related.

The problems London faces are the symptoms. Khan is the cause.

items.title: First Thing: Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic trilateral meeting in China

The three leaders spoke about international peace and nuclear weapons as Trump called Putin a ‘friend’. Plus, yes, GTA VI is really finally here, and the critics have their verdict: masterpiece

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Donald Trump has met Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, and said the three leaders were “really making history”. The trilateral meeting lasted roughly an hour and a half, according to Chinese state media. On arrival the US president described his Russian counterpart as “my friend”.

Putin told Xi and Trump that their countries shared “many converging interests” when it came to resolving conflicts, including the full-scale war in Ukraine, which the Russian president started in 2022.

What was unusual about China’s welcome to the Japanese delegation? Apec’s Chinese hosts went out of their way to give world leaders a warm welcome as they arrived in Shenzhen, with one exception. Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, had to make do with a modest guard of honour and a welcome from a relatively junior Chinese government official.

The Guardian is live blogging the Apec summit. You can follow it here.

What is the latest warning on the environmental impact of AI? The world’s datacentres will create 70% more carbon emissions within the next four years as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI growth agendas, according to the world’s energy watchdog.

Who has been accused of spying in Silicon Valley? The US Department of Justice has accused a Russian national of spying on employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company in an alleged effort to gather intelligence for Russia. Igor D’iu had been indicted on multiple charges.

Why have four Maryland high school students sued after an AI error? Four current and former students at a Maryland high school have filed a lawsuit a year after armed police detained them, prompted by an AI alert that mistook a bag of Doritos for a gun, in an incident that left them “fearing for their lives”.
